After the marriage, CW1 was residing at house No.21/1, Adi Kabir Ashrama Road, II Cross, Near V Care Hospital, Motinagar within the limits of R. T. to the accused No.1 on several occasions.
The accused No.1 had taken away gold chain weighing 25 grams belongs to CW1.

On 21-11- 2022, the accused no.1 at the instigation of accused No.2 and 3 under the influence of alcohol abused CW1 with filthiest language, beaten her with hands and threatened her by stating that he will kill CW1 and her family.

After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused No.1 to 3, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A), 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code has been framed, read over and explained to the accused persons in the language known to them, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 8 witnesses and examined 1 witness and exhibited 5 documents.

The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Nandini and accused No.1 was solemnized on 07-12-2020 and thereafter started residing at house No.21/1, Adi Kabir Ashrama Road, 2nd Cross, Near V Care KABC030087272023 CC No.5443/2023 Hospital, Motinagar within the limits of R.T. Nagara Police Station, Bangalore at that time the accused No.1 at the instigation of accused No.2 and 3 with common intention subjected the CW1 to mental and physical cruelty for fetching additional dowry amount thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.498(A) read with Sec.34 of IPC?
2.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 21-11-2022, at above mentioned place, the accused no.1 at the instigation of accused No.2 and 3 in furtherance of common intention abused CW1 with filthiest language knowingly such abusive words will provoke breach of peace thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec. 504 read with Sec.34 of IPC?
KABC030087272023 CC No.5443/2023 3.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said duration, the accused No.1 at the instigation of accused No.2 and 3 in furtherance of common intention beaten CW1 with his hands and caused simple hurt thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.323 read with Sec.34 of IPC?
4. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said duration, the accused No.1 at the instigation of accused No.2 and 3 in furtherance of common intention threatened CW1 with dire consequences thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.506 read with Sec.34 of IPC?
5.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said KABC030087272023 CC No.5443/2023 duration, the accused No.1 at the instigation of accused No.2 and 3 harassed CW1 to fetch additional dowry amount from her parental house and received Rs.1,10,000/- from CW1 and had taken her 5 grams of gold chain thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
6.
What order?

13. The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1-5 : In the Negative Point No.6 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1 to 5: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the KABC030087272023 CC No.5443/2023 prosecution has examined one witness,

4 which is as follows:
i. CW1 by name Smt. Nandini being informant examined as PW1 and identified her signatures on Ex.P1 (Complaint) and Ex.P2(Spot Mahazar) as Ex.P1(a) and 2(a)
deposed that when she went to the police station for sorting out the minor differences of opinion amongst her and the accused persons, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 and further stated that she did not lodge complaint against accused persons and no mahazar was conducted in her presence.

sentences.text: In this regard, the learned Sr.APP cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.

Her denial statement given before the police is marked as per Ex.P3.
15.

The certified copies of Memorandum of Settlement and order sheet of MC No.6729/2022 are marked as Ex.P4 and Ex.P5 respectively.

On perusal of the above recital, it is appear that the disputes between the accused No.1 and CW1 (informant)
have been settled and they are living together.

16. This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana and anr in the case of AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

and in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat),
wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the KABC030087272023 CC No.5443/2023 matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused No.1 have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498(A), 323, 504, 506 of IPC and Sec.4 of D.P. Act is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".
18.

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
Under these circumstances, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the ingredients for offences Under Section 498(A), 323, 504, 506 of IPC and Sec.4 of D.P. Act was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answer the point No.1 to 5 in the Negative.

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 5, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused No.1 to 3 are found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A), 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
(ii) Accused are set at liberty.

(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C their bail bonds shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
(iv) Ordered accordingly.
